200: Saint Seiya: Saintia Sho by Chimaki Kuori (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action story set in the world of Saint Seiya. Shoko is an ordinary, hot-headed girl until her older sister Kyoko is taken by the goddess Eris. To get her back, Shoko joins the Saintia, the female warriors sworn to guard the goddess Athena. It's a good pick for fans of the original series and anyone who likes armored heroines and big battles.
201: Wolf Girl and Black Prince by Ayuko Hatta (Viz Media) is a high school romantic comedy built on one small lie. Erika Shinohara wants to fit in with her friends, so she claims to have a boyfriend and backs it up with a photo of a handsome stranger. When he turns out to be Kyoya Sata from her own school, he agrees to play along, on the condition that she becomes his loyal "dog." Readers who like prickly, push-and-pull romances will feel at home.
203: Yamada-kun and the Seven Witches by Miki Yoshikawa (Kodansha) is a school romantic comedy with a supernatural twist. Ryu Yamada is a delinquent with bad grades and no friends, until he tumbles down the stairs with Urara Shiraishi, the top student in school, and the two wake up in each other's bodies. Their swap leads them into the school's secret of the seven witches. It's lively and funny, with a mystery thread running underneath.
204: Magical Girl Apocalypse by Kentaro Sato (Seven Seas) is a horror action story that turns magical girls into a nightmare. Kii Kogami is a shy high school otaku who would rather be left alone. Then one ordinary school day, murderous magical girls appear and start slaughtering everyone in sight, leaving Kii and a handful of classmates fighting to survive. Expect fast pacing and plenty of gore, so it's best for readers who like intense survival horror.
205: Magical Girl Site by Kentaro Sato (Seven Seas) is a dark psychological horror story. Aya Asagiri is bullied at school and miserable at home, and she has started to wish she could just disappear. Then a strange website called the Magical Girl Site appears on her screen and hands her a "stick" with real power, pulling her into a deadly world of other magical girls. It's grim and violent, best for fans of dark takes on the genre.
206: Your Lie in April by Naoshi Arakawa (Kodansha) is a drama about music, grief, and first love. Kosei Arima was a child piano prodigy until his mother's death left him unable to hear his own playing. Now in middle school, he has given up music, until he meets Kaori Miyazono, a free-spirited violinist who drags him back toward the stage. It's heartfelt and bittersweet, a good pick for readers who like emotional stories with real warmth.
207: Malevolent Spirits: Mononogatari by Onigunsou (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action story about the spirits that live inside old objects. Hyoma Kunato is a young exorcist with a deep grudge against tsukumogami. He is sent to Kyoto to live with Botan Ise, a girl who shares her home with a whole family of them, and living under one roof forces him to rethink what he believes. It mixes stylish battles with found-family warmth.
209: So I'm a Spider, So What? by Okina Baba (Yen Press) is a fantasy light novel series with a very unusual hero. After a mysterious explosion wipes out her high school class, one girl is reborn in another world as a tiny spider monster at the bottom of a dungeon full of creatures that want to eat her. Her upbeat inner voice keeps the survival story funny. Fans of offbeat isekai and game-style leveling will have a great time.
210: So I'm a Spider, So What? by Okina Baba (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure adapted from the light novel series, with art by Asahiro Kakashi. After a mysterious explosion wipes out her high school class, one girl is reborn in another world as a tiny spider monster, stranded deep in a dungeon full of hungry monsters. Her upbeat, chatty inner voice makes the struggle to survive funny. It's a fun entry point for isekai fans.
211: Kageki Shojo!! by Kumiko Saiki (Seven Seas) is a coming-of-age drama set in the world of all-female musical theater. Sarasa Watanabe is tall, cheerful, and set on playing a leading man on stage. She enrolls in the elite Kouka School of Musical Theater, where she rooms with Ai Narata, a guarded former idol, among equally driven classmates. It's a warm, thoughtful story about ambition and friendship, a good pick for readers who love performing-arts stories.
213: Overlord by Kugane Maruyama (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy light novel series told from the villain's side. On the final night of a popular online game, a player stays logged in as his skeletal sorcerer avatar, Momonga. When the servers should shut down, the game world becomes real instead, and the characters in his guild now serve him. Readers who enjoy antihero isekai and grand strategy will like watching him figure out this new world.
214: The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity by Saka Mikami (Kodansha) is a gentle high school romance. Rintaro Tsumugi goes to a rough-and-tumble boys' school, and next door is an elite girls' academy, where the students look down on his school. When he meets Kaoruko Waguri, a kind girl from that academy, she treats him without any prejudice at all. It's sweet and sincere, a good choice for readers who like slow, kind-hearted love stories.
215: Boarding School Juliet by Yousuke Kaneda (Kodansha) is a Romeo-and-Juliet romantic comedy set at a boarding school. Students from two rival nations, the Black Doggies and the White Cats, share one campus and fight constantly. Romio Inuzuka, leader of the first-year Black Doggies, has a secret crush on Juliet Persia, the White Cats' proud leader, and when he finally confesses, the two begin a secret relationship. It's funny and big-hearted, great for fans of forbidden-love comedies.
216: Suppose a Kid from the Last Dungeon Boonies Moved to a Starter Town by Toshio Satou (Yen Press) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy light novel. Lloyd Belladonna grew up in a remote village and thinks of himself as the weakest kid there. He heads to the capital to chase his dream of becoming a soldier, never realizing his hometown sits next to the world's last dungeon and that, by ordinary standards, he is incredibly strong. Fans of feel-good overpowered heroes will enjoy it.
218: Tail of the Moon by Rinko Ueda (Viz Media) is a historical romantic comedy about a ninja in training. Usagi is a sweet but hopeless kunoichi whose skills are mostly limited to herbal medicine. Her village gives her one mission: travel to the feared ninja Hanzo Hattori and convince him to father her child, a future ninja heir, even though Hanzo is not interested. It's playful and romantic, a nice pick for readers who like shojo set in feudal Japan.
219: Monster Musume: Everyday Life with Monster Girls by OKAYADO (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy with a heavy dose of fan service. In a world where monster girls have just been brought into human society through an exchange program, ordinary student Kimihito Kurusu is assigned a host-family guest: Miia, a clingy lamia. More monster girls soon move in, and his household gets very crowded. It's silly and cheeky, best for older teens and adults who like harem comedies.
220: Tearmoon Empire by Nozomu Mochitsuki (J-Novel Club) is a comedic fantasy light novel series about a princess on her second chance. Mia Luna Tearmoon was a spoiled imperial princess whose empire collapsed, ending with her on the guillotine. Then she wakes up as her twelve-year-old self, holding the diary she kept during that lost life, and sets out to avoid the blade. Her selfish schemes keep getting mistaken for brilliance, which is half the fun.
221: Tegami Bachi: Letter Bee by Hiroyuki Asada (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure set in a land of perpetual night. Letter Bees are couriers who brave monster-filled wilderness to carry people's letters and parcels, and Lag Seeing knows this firsthand: as a little boy he was mailed as a package himself, delivered by a Bee named Gauche Suede. Now Lag wants to become a Letter Bee too. It's moving and beautifully drawn, a good choice for fans of heartfelt adventure.
222: +Anima by Natsumi Mukai (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure about kids with animal powers. In this world, some children are +Anima, able to take on the abilities of animals and often feared for it. Cooro, a cheerful boy who can sprout crow wings, travels with a small group of other +Anima looking for a place to belong, each of them carrying a painful past. It's gentle and charming, a good pick for younger readers and found-family fans.
223: Animal Land by Makoto Raiku (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure set in a world ruled by animals. A tanuki named Monoko finds an abandoned human baby by the river and decides to raise him, naming him Taroza. Taroza turns out to have a special gift: he can speak with every kind of animal, in a world where predators and prey can't understand each other. It's a big-hearted story about kindness and survival, with real stakes behind the cute faces.
224: Gravitation by Maki Murakami (Tokyopop) is a boys' love romantic comedy set in the music industry. Shuichi Shindo is the excitable lead singer of the up-and-coming band Bad Luck. One night he loses a page of his lyrics, and the stranger who picks it up, famous romance novelist Eiri Yuki, tells him bluntly that he has no talent. Shuichi can't stop thinking about him, and the result is chaotic, over-the-top, and a classic of early BL.
225: Atom: The Beginning by Tetsuro Kasahara and Masami Yuki (Titan Manga), based on Osamu Tezuka's Astro Boy, is a science fiction drama about the robot before the legend. In a Japan rebuilding after a disaster, two brilliant young researchers, Umataro Tenma and Hiroshi Ochanomizu, work out of a cramped university lab. Their latest creation, a robot called A106, shows signs of something like a mind of its own. It's a thoughtful prequel for Tezuka fans and robot-story lovers.
226: Bamboo Blade by Masahiro Totsuka with art by Aguri Igarashi (Yen Press) is a sports comedy about a high school kendo club. Toraji Ishida is a broke, slacker kendo coach who bets his old upperclassman a year of free sushi that his girls' team can win a match, even though he barely has a team. Then he meets Tamaki Kawazoe, a quiet girl with real talent. It's easygoing and funny, with heart.
227: The Law of Ueki by Tsubasa Fukuchi (Viz Media) is a supernatural action story about a tournament of strange powers. Kosuke Ueki is a middle schooler with a strong sense of justice and an odd ability: he can turn trash into trees. His teacher gave him that power as a candidate in a secret battle among middle school kids to choose the next celestial king, and classmate Ai Mori gets swept into it with him. It's goofy and creative, a nice classic battle manga.
229: The Vexations of a Shut-In Vampire Princess by Kotei Kobayashi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel series. Terakomari Gandesblood is a vampire who can't stand the sight of blood and would rather stay in her room forever. Then she is forced to command an army of bloodthirsty brutes who only respect strength, so she has to bluff her way through, pretending to be terrifyingly powerful. It's bubbly and silly, great for fans of cute misunderstanding comedies.
232: Cardcaptor Sakura: Clear Card by CLAMP (Kodansha) is a magical girl fantasy and the sequel to Cardcaptor Sakura. Sakura Kinomoto is starting junior high, and Syaoran has finally come back to Tomoeda. But after a strange dream, all of her Sakura Cards turn clear and lose their power, and new, mysterious cards begin appearing around town. It's sweet and gorgeously drawn, perfect for longtime fans of the original series.
234: To the Abandoned Sacred Beasts by Maybe (Vertical) is a dark fantasy action story about soldiers left behind after a war. During a civil war, the North turned volunteers into Incarnates, monstrous super-soldiers who helped win the fight but began losing their humanity once peace came. Hank, their former commander, now hunts them down one by one, and Schaal Bancroft, the daughter of one of his targets, insists on joining him. It's somber and thoughtful, for readers who like moral weight.
235: Tokyo Ghoul by Sui Ishida (Viz Media) is a horror action story set in a Tokyo where flesh-eating ghouls live hidden among people. Ken Kaneki is a shy college student who finally lands a date with Rize, a girl he admires. The evening ends in a brutal attack, and Kaneki wakes up in a hospital with her organs transplanted into him, now half ghoul and craving human flesh. It's dark, stylish, and violent, a modern horror favorite.
237: City by Keiichi Arawi (Vertical) is an absurdist slice-of-life comedy from the creator of Nichijou. It follows the residents of a small town called City, starting with Midori Nagumo, a college student who is always broke and always scheming to get by. Her friends, neighbors, the local diner staff, and even the police are just as strange as she is, and the everyday chaos piles up in surprising ways. It's light and playful, ideal for fans of offbeat gag comedies.
238: Tuxedo Gin by Tokihiko Matsuura (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a supernatural twist. Ginji Kusanagi is a young boxer who finally gets a date with Minako, the girl of his dreams, but he is killed in an accident on his way there. Given a chance to earn his life back, he is reborn as a penguin and adopted by Minako, and now he has to protect her without being able to say a word. It's silly, warm, and surprisingly touching.
239: Vampire Game by Judal (Tokyopop) is a fantasy comedy about a vampire king plotting revenge in an unusual body. Long ago, the vampire king Duzell was slain by King Phelios, and now he has been reborn as a cute little kitten, determined to kill Phelios's descendants. He ends up in the arms of Princess Ishtar, who has very different plans for her new pet. It's witty and lighthearted, with royal intrigue and plenty of bickering, a fun pick for fans of classic shojo fantasy.
240: Reign of the Seven Spellblades by Bokuto Uno (Yen Press) is a fantasy action light novel series set at a dangerous magic school. Oliver Horn arrives at Kimberly Magic Academy, a prestigious school where students die every year in pursuit of power. On his first day he meets Nanao Hibiya, a samurai girl from a faraway land, and other new classmates who quickly become a close group, while Oliver hides a secret purpose of his own. It's a dark twist on the magic-academy story.
241: Vinland Saga by Makoto Yukimura (Kodansha) is a historical drama set in the age of the Vikings. As a boy in Iceland, Thorfinn sees his father Thors, a legendary warrior, killed by the mercenary Askeladd. Thorfinn grows up inside Askeladd's own crew, fighting for him in hopes of earning a duel and his revenge. It's rich and mature, and it slowly widens into a reflection on violence and what it means to be a true warrior.
242: Knights of Sidonia by Tsutomu Nihei (Vertical) is a science fiction action story aboard a ship carrying the last of humanity. A thousand years after alien creatures called the Gauna destroyed Earth, the colony ship Sidonia drifts through space. Nagate Tanikaze has lived his whole life hidden in its underground levels, and when he finally surfaces, he is trained to pilot the Guardian mechs that fight the Gauna. It's tense and atmospheric, a good pick for hard sci-fi and mecha fans.
243: Rosario+Vampire: Season II by Akihisa Ikeda (Viz Media) is a supernatural action comedy and the continuation of Rosario+Vampire. Tsukune Aono is still the only human attending Yokai Academy, a school for monsters, and he still has to keep that a secret. As his second year begins, he and his friends in the newspaper club, including the vampire Moka Akashiya, face new threats. It mixes harem comedy with bigger battles, and it's best for readers who finished the first series.
244: Devils and Realist by Madoka Takadono with art by Utako Yukihiro (Seven Seas) is a supernatural comedy set at an English boarding school. William Twining is a practical, sharp-tongued student who doesn't believe in anything supernatural. When his family's fortune collapses, he searches his house for treasure and accidentally summons the demon Dantalion, who claims William is the descendant of King Solomon and must choose the next ruler of Hell. It's witty and stylish, with plenty of banter.
246: Loner Life in Another World by Shoji Goji (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy light novel series. A whole high school class is summoned to another world, and each student gets to pick special skills from a god. Haruka is a loner who shows up last, so he is stuck with the leftover skills nobody wanted and left on his own in the wilderness to make them work. It's quirky, with lots of sarcastic humor.
247: She Professed Herself Pupil of the Wise Man by Ryusen Hirotsugu (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy light novel series. Kagami Sakimori plays a VR game as Danblf, a famous elderly summoner wizard. While fiddling with a feature that changes his avatar's appearance, he falls asleep and wakes up inside the game world as a cute young girl, and rather than admit who he is, he claims to be Danblf's pupil. It's breezy and fun for fans of game-world isekai.
248: Shomin Sample by Takafumi Nanatsuki (Seven Seas) is a school romantic comedy about a culture clash. Kimito Kagurazaka is an ordinary high school boy who is abducted and taken to an elite all-girls academy. The sheltered young ladies there have never met a commoner, so he has been brought in as a "sample" to teach them about everyday life, and he has to play the part carefully or face expulsion. It's goofy fun, for readers who like fish-out-of-water comedy.
249: So Cute It Hurts!! by Go Ikeyamada (Viz Media) is a twin-swap romantic comedy. Megumu is a girl who loves otaku hobbies, and her twin brother Mitsuru is a popular charmer. To help each other out, they agree to trade places for a while, and while disguised as her brother at his tough boys' school, Megumu ends up falling for one of his classmates. It's bubbly and fun, perfect for fans of cross-dressing hijinks.
250: Spiral: The Bonds of Reasoning by Kyo Shirodaira with art by Eita Mizuno (Yen Press) is a mystery thriller full of mind games. Ayumu Narumi's brilliant detective brother, Kiyotaka, disappeared without a trace, leaving only a cryptic mention of the "Blade Children." When Ayumu is accused of murder, he must use his own sharp reasoning to clear his name. It's tense and clever, a good pick for readers who love puzzles.
251: Otherside Picnic by Iori Miyazawa (Square Enix) is a science fiction horror story adapted from the light novels. College student Sorawo Kamikoshi has been exploring the Otherside, an eerie parallel world full of creatures straight out of internet urban legends. On one trip she nearly drowns and is rescued by Toriko Nishina, a striking woman searching for her missing friend, and the two become exploring partners. It's creepy and quietly romantic, for fans of strange, unsettling stories.
252: Library Wars: Love & War by Kiiro Yumi (Viz Media), based on the novels by Hiro Arikawa, is a romantic action story about the fight for free speech. In a future Japan, the government censors books by force, and libraries keep their own armed defense force to protect them. Iku Kasahara joins up, inspired by a mysterious officer who once saved a book for her, only to clash with her strict instructor, Dojo. It's fun, sweet, and thoughtful.
254: My Next Life as a Villainess: All Routes Lead to Doom! by Satoru Yamaguchi (J-Novel Club) is a comedic romance light novel series. As a young noble girl, Katarina Claes bumps her head and remembers her past life. She realizes she has been reborn as the villainess of an otome game she used to play, where every ending leads to her exile or death, so she sets out to avoid her fate and wins hearts without noticing. It's sunny and silly.
255: A Sister's All You Need. by Yomi Hirasaka (Yen Press) is a comedy light novel series about the life of a young writer. Itsuki Hashima is a light novelist with one big obsession, little sisters, and he writes about them constantly. He spends his days with an odd circle of fellow creatives, including a talented novelist who is openly in love with him. It's a cheeky look inside the publishing world, best for older readers who like offbeat comedies about creators.
256: Strawberry 100% by Mizuki Kawashita (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy about a boy with too many crushes. Middle schooler Junpei Manaka is on the school rooftop when a mysterious girl falls on him and runs off, leaving him only a glimpse of her strawberry-print underwear. He becomes determined to find out who she is, and soon several girls are in his life. It's lighthearted, with plenty of fan service, for fans of classic harem rom-coms.
258: Adachi and Shimamura by Hitoma Iruma (Seven Seas) is a yuri romance light novel series. Shimamura and Adachi are two high school girls who start cutting class and hanging out in the same quiet spot on the gym's second floor, playing ping-pong and talking about nothing much. For Shimamura it's an easy friendship, but Adachi finds herself feeling a lot more. It's slow, introspective, and gentle, a good pick for fans of quiet romance.
259: Gakuen Alice by Tachibana Higuchi (Tokyopop) is a fantasy comedy about a school for kids with special powers. Mikan Sakura is a cheerful country girl whose best friend Hotaru leaves to attend Alice Academy, a school for children with gifts called Alices. Mikan follows her to Tokyo and discovers she has an Alice of her own, though school life there is not as wonderful as it seems. It's bright and fun, with darker secrets underneath.
261: My Love Story!! by Kazune Kawahara with art by Aruko (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a gentle giant at its heart. Takeo Gouda is huge, strong, and kind, but girls always fall for his handsome best friend, Sunakawa, instead. When Takeo rescues a sweet girl named Yamato from a groper on the train, he assumes she likes Sunakawa too, but he's wrong. It's heartwarming and funny, a good choice for anyone who wants a feel-good love story.
262: The Dangers in My Heart by Norio Sakurai (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about an awkward middle schooler. Kyotaro Ichikawa is a gloomy loner who daydreams about dark things, and he has picked Anna Yamada, the class's tall, popular model, as the target of his grim fantasies. But the more he watches her, the more he discovers she is goofy, kind, and not at all what he expected. It's sweet and funny, for fans of slow-burn school romance.
263: Nabari no Ou by Yuhki Kamatani (Yen Press) is a supernatural action drama about the hidden world of ninja. Miharu Rokujo is an apathetic middle schooler who doesn't care about much, until he learns that he carries the Shinra Banshou, a secret ninja art that grants unlimited power to whoever controls it. With rival ninja villages after him, his teacher and a classmate decide to protect him. It's moody and thoughtful, for readers who like character-driven ninja stories.
264: Naruto by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a ninja action story about a boy determined to be noticed. Naruto Uzumaki is a loud, troublemaking orphan in the Hidden Leaf Village, shunned because a nine-tailed fox demon is sealed inside him. He dreams of becoming Hokage, the village's strongest ninja, and begins training alongside Sasuke and Sakura to get there. The omnibus format makes this classic easy to collect.
265: The Dungeon of Black Company by Youhei Yasumura (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy about a man whose easy life is turned upside down. Kinji Ninomiya earned enough money to never work again and planned to live as a happy shut-in. Then he is transported to another world and forced into a brutal job mining dungeons for a shady company, where he refuses to stay at the bottom. It's a sharp satire of corporate life, funny and cynical.
266: The Great Cleric by Broccoli Lion (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure adapted from the web novel series. After dying, a young man is reborn in a world of swords and magic as Luciel. He chooses healing magic, figuring a healer is the safest path, and joins the Adventurers' Guild to learn, only to find his training is brutally hard work. It's steady and earnest, a good choice for readers who like slow-growth heroes and fantasy training arcs.
267: Beet the Vandel Buster by Riku Sanjo with art by Koji Inada (Viz Media) is a classic fantasy adventure. In a world terrorized by monstrous Vandels, young Beet dreams of becoming a Vandel Buster, one of the heroes who fight back. After an attack leaves him with the weapons of his fallen idols, the Zenon Warriors, he sets out to finish what they started. It's bright and action-packed, from the same writer as Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai.
269: I Was Reincarnated as the 7th Prince So I Can Take My Time Perfecting My Magical Ability by Kenkyo na Circle (Kodansha) is a fantasy action series. A commoner sorcerer who loved magic dies before he can master it and is reborn as Lloyd, the seventh prince of a kingdom. Far from the throne, he can finally devote his life to studying magic, and his abilities are frightening. It's breezy and fun for fans of overpowered heroes.
270: Bride of the Water God by Mi-Kyung Yun (Dark Horse) is a fantasy romance drawn from Korean legend. Soah is a young woman chosen by her drought-stricken village as a sacrifice to Habaek, the water god. Instead of dying, she arrives in his kingdom and finds that her new husband appears to be a little boy, and the longer she stays, the more she learns about him. It's lush and beautifully illustrated, a lovely choice for readers who like mythic romances.
271: Platinum End by Tsugumi Ohba with art by Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a supernatural thriller from the creators of Death Note. Mirai Kakehashi has lost all hope and tries to end his life, but he is caught by an angel named Nasse. She gives him supernatural powers and tells him he is a candidate to become the next god, and the other candidates soon start hunting each other. It's dark and suspenseful, for readers who like moral battles.
272: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? On the Side: Sword Oratoria by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy action light novel series. This spinoff follows Ais Wallenstein, the elite swordswoman known as the Sword Princess, and her powerful Loki Familia as they explore the dungeon beneath Orario. While she grows stronger, new threats rise from the depths. It's a great companion for fans of the main series who want more of Ais's side.
273: Prison School by Akira Hiramoto (Yen Press) is an outrageous comedy for mature readers. Hachimitsu Academy was an elite all-girls boarding school until it began admitting boys, and only five have enrolled. When they get caught peeping in the girls' bath, the student council's secret Underground Council throws them into the school's own prison, and their escape plans only make things worse. It's crude and very funny, for adults who like over-the-top humor.
275: Trigun Maximum by Yasuhiro Nightow (Dark Horse) is a sci-fi western action story and the continuation of Trigun. On a desert planet, Vash the Stampede is a gunslinger with a huge bounty on his head who refuses to kill. After two years in hiding he reappears, with a new band of killers, the Gung-Ho Guns, coming after him and insurance agents Meryl and Milly back on his trail. It's stylish and full of heart.
276: Crimson Hero by Mitsuba Takanashi (Viz Media) is a sports romance about a girl who lives for volleyball. Nobara Sumiyoshi is a tall, determined girl whose family wants her to become the refined heir to their restaurant. She picked her high school for its volleyball team, only to learn the girls' team has been shut down, so she takes a job as dorm mother for the boys' team to stay. It's spirited and fun for sports fans.
278: Karneval by Touya Mikanagi (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story about an unlikely pair. Nai is a sweet, naive boy searching for Karoku, the person who took care of him, and Gareki is a hardened young thief. When their paths cross, both get caught up with Circus, a national defense organization that fights monsters, and Nai's bracelet turns out to matter a great deal. It's colorful and stylish, with a warm found-family heart.
279: Uzaki-chan Wants to Hang Out! by Take (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about a loner and the girl who won't let him be alone. Shinichi Sakurai is a college student who likes his quiet time, but Hana Uzaki, his loud, energetic underclassman from high school, is determined to drag him out to have fun. Their teasing back-and-forth slowly turns into something more. It's light and silly, with fan service, for fans of teasing romances.
280: Vampire Dormitory by Ema Toyama (Kodansha) is a supernatural romance with a gender-disguise twist. Mito Yamamoto has lost her home and has nowhere to go, so she disguises herself as a boy. She ends up taking a deal from Ruka, a handsome vampire who wants her blood in exchange for a place in an all-boys dorm, and keeping her secret gets complicated quickly. It's dramatic and flirty, a nice pick for paranormal shojo fans.
281: Waiting for Spring by Anashin (Kodansha) is a sweet high school romance. Mitsuki Haruno is a shy girl who wants to make friends after a lonely middle school life. Her plans take an unexpected turn when four popular boys from the basketball team start hanging around the cafe where she works, and one of them, Towa, seems especially interested in her. It's gentle and cheerful, a nice pick for readers who like warm, low-drama shojo.
282: Wandance by Coffee (Kodansha) is a coming-of-age drama about street dance. Kaboku Kotani is a high school student with a stutter who has learned to keep quiet and blend in. Then he sees his classmate Hikari Wanda dancing alone, completely lost in the music, and joins the dance club to chase that feeling himself. It's kinetic and heartfelt, a great pick for readers who love underdog stories and art that moves.
283: Kurohime by Masanori Katakura (Viz Media) is a fantasy western action story. Kurohime is a fearsome gun-slinging witch who has insulted the gods one too many times. As punishment, they turn her into a sweet, helpless girl who can only return to her true form through love, and a young man named Zero is the one who first brings her back. It's flashy and fun, with lots of gunfights and magic.
284: Saiyuki Reload by Kazuya Minekura (Tokyopop) is a fantasy action story and the continuation of Saiyuki. The monk Genjo Sanzo is still traveling west on his mission, joined by his three demon companions: the cheerful Goku, the flirtatious Gojyo, and the polite but dangerous Hakkai. Along the road, they face new attacks from assassins. It's stylish, irreverent, and full of brotherly banter, best for readers who finished the original series.
285: Devils' Line by Ryo Hanada (Vertical) is a supernatural romance thriller about vampires living among humans. In this world, vampires called devils can lose control at the sight of blood. College student Tsukasa Taira is rescued from one by Yuki Anzai, a half-vampire who works with a special police unit hunting rogue devils, and the two are drawn to each other despite the danger. It's dark, mature, and tense, for older readers who like gritty paranormal romance.
286: Sayonara, Zetsubou-Sensei by Koji Kumeta (Kodansha) is a satirical comedy about a teacher in endless despair. Nozomu Itoshiki is a high school teacher who finds everything hopeless, and on his way to his first day he meets Kafuka Fuura, a relentlessly positive student who sees the good in everything. His class is full of quirky, troubled students, and each chapter skewers Japanese society with dark wit. It's sharp and very funny, for fans of offbeat gag comedy.
287: School Rumble by Jin Kobayashi (Del Rey) is a high school romantic comedy built on a chain of crushes. Tenma Tsukamoto is cheerful and clumsy, and she can't work up the nerve to confess to her strange classmate Karasuma. Meanwhile, Kenji Harima is the school's toughest delinquent, and he is hopelessly in love with Tenma. It's wild, warm, and funny, a beloved classic for fans of ensemble comedies.
288: Love and Lies by Musawo (Kodansha) is a romantic drama set in a future where love is assigned. In Japan, everyone is matched with a government-chosen partner at sixteen, and dating anyone else is forbidden. Yukari Nejima confesses to his crush, Misaki Takasaki, on the night before his sixteenth birthday, just before his official match arrives. It's heartfelt and bittersweet, for readers who like love triangles with big questions.
289: Love of Kill by Fe (Yen Press) is an action romance about a bounty hunter and an assassin. Chateau Dankworth is a skilled bounty hunter, and Song Ryang is a cheerful, deadly assassin who has taken an unsettling interest in her. He keeps turning up when she needs him, but she can't tell if he wants to help her or kill her. It's tense and darkly flirtatious, a great pick for fans of dangerous romances.
291: Loveless by Yun Kouga (Tokyopop) is a dark fantasy drama set in a world where people keep cat ears until they lose their innocence. Ritsuka Aoyagi is a twelve-year-old boy struggling after his older brother Seimei was murdered. Then a young man named Soubi appears, claiming he knew Seimei, and pulls Ritsuka into a secret world of spell battles fought in pairs. It's moody and emotionally intense, for older readers who like atmospheric, mysterious stories.
292: Dragon Drive by Ken-ichi Sakura (Viz Media) is an action fantasy adventure. Reiji Ozora is a boy who gives up on everything, until his friend Maiko gets him to try Dragon Drive, a virtual reality game where players battle with dragon partners. His dragon, Chibi, looks small and useless at first, but Reiji soon finds out the game is connected to a real world. It's energetic and easy to get into, a fun pick for younger readers who love monster battles.
293: Yuri Is My Job! by Miman (Kodansha) is a workplace romantic comedy. Hime Shiraki keeps up a carefully crafted, princess-like public persona, but after she accidentally injures the manager of a café, she has to fill in there. The café, Liebe, is staged like an elite girls' school, where staff play refined students, and her new partner, Mitsuki, sees right through her act. It's playful and full of drama, great for fans of yuri romance.
294: Eden: It's an Endless World! by Hiroki Endo (Dark Horse) is a science fiction action drama for mature readers. A deadly virus has wiped out much of humanity, and the survivors live in a world reshaped by war and powerful organizations. Elijah Ballard is a teenager who travels with a combat robot, caught up in that dangerous world while searching for answers. It's violent, smart, and philosophical, a strong pick for adult readers who like gritty, thoughtful sci-fi.
295: Maximum Ride by James Patterson with art by NaRae Lee (Yen Press) is a science fiction action story adapted from the bestselling novels. Max is a fourteen-year-old girl who, like the five other members of her Flock, was created in a lab and given wings. The kids escaped the scientists who made them and live in hiding, until the youngest, Angel, is kidnapped and Max has to go after her. It's fast-moving and fun, good for teen readers.
296: Special A by Maki Minami (Viz Media) is a school romantic comedy about a fierce rivalry. Hikari Hanazono has always been second best to Kei Takishima, a cool, wealthy genius who beat her at wrestling when they were kids. Now at an elite academy, she is determined to beat him at something, never noticing that he likes her. Their friends in the top-ranked Special A class make it even livelier, and the whole thing is fun and sweet.
